turns.prompt_text: What is the apple app where I may draw text and it cleans it up?
turns.response_html:
The app you're looking for is most likely Apple Notes, though the functionality is also built into Freeform.

Depending on exactly how you want the text "cleaned up," Apple offers two distinct features for this, primarily on the iPad:

1. Smart Script (Handwriting Refinement)

If you want your handwriting to stay as handwriting but look much neater, this is the feature for you. Introduced in iPadOS 18, it uses on-device machine learning to "clean up" your writing in real-time.

  • How it works: As you write with an Apple Pencil, the app smooths out your strokes and straightens your lines while maintaining your personal style.
  • Manual Clean-up: You can also select a block of messy handwriting you've already written, tap it, and select "Refine" to instantly neaten it.

2. Scribble (Handwriting to Typed Text)

If "cleaning it up" means converting your drawings into actual typed computer font, that feature is called Scribble.

  • How it works: You can write with your Apple Pencil in any text field (including the body of a Note), and it will instantly transform into typed text.
  • Where to find it: It’s enabled by default in Settings > Apple Pencil > Scribble.

Other "Cleanup" Features

  • Shape Recognition: If you draw a shape (like a circle or arrow) and hold the Pencil down at the end, the app will "snap" it into a perfect, clean geometric shape.
  • Math Notes: In the Notes app, if you write out a math equation (like $2x + 5 = 15$), the app can "clean it up" by solving it for you in your own handwriting style.

Pro Tip: If you're using an iPhone or Mac without an Apple Pencil, you can still use Writing Tools (part of Apple Intelligence) to clean up the tone and grammar of text you've already typed.

Are you using an iPad with an Apple Pencil, or are you looking for a way to do this on your iPhone?

turns.prompt_text: Is this feature available in concepts?
turns.response_html:
The short answer is no, the specific "Smart Script" feature (which makes your messy handwriting look like a neater version of your own handwriting) is currently exclusive to Apple Notes and Freeform.

However, Concepts—being a professional vector-based illustration app—has its own set of "cleanup" tools that work a bit differently:

1. Line Smoothing (Real-Time Cleanup)

Concepts is famous for its Smoothing slider. Instead of cleaning up the text after you write it, you can set the smoothing (anywhere from 0% to 100%) to stabilize your strokes as you draw them.

  • Low Smoothing (10-20%): Removes the "jitters" from your hand while keeping your natural handwriting style.
  • High Smoothing (100%): Turns every stroke into a perfectly smooth curve or a straight line.

2. Shape Recognition

Like Apple Notes, Concepts has a Shape Recognition feature. If you draw a rough circle, square, or line and hold your stylus down for a second at the end, it will "snap" into a perfect geometric shape. You can enable this in Settings > Interaction > Draw & Hold.

3. Apple "Scribble" Support

Concepts does support the system-wide Scribble feature, but only when you are using the Text Tool.

  • If you select the Text Tool and tap on the canvas, a text box appears.
  • You can write inside that box with your Apple Pencil, and iPadOS will convert it into typed text.
  • Note: Unlike Apple Notes, you cannot just write anywhere on the infinite canvas and have it automatically turn into typed text; it has to be done through that specific text input flow.

4. Vector Manipulation

The biggest advantage of Concepts is that every stroke is a vector. This means if you write a word and it looks "messy," you can select the individual strokes and:

  • Nudge them: Use the "Nudge" tool to physically push parts of the letters around to make them look better.
  • Change the tool: You can select your messy handwriting and change the brush type or thickness after the fact to make it look cleaner.

Summary: If you want that magical "automatic neat handwriting" effect, you'll need to stay in Apple Notes. If you want precise control over smoothing out your strokes as you draw, Concepts is the better tool.

Do you primarily use Concepts for quick note-taking, or are you using it for more technical design work?
